questions.q: Which one of the following is the oldest group of rocks in India?
questions.e: Archaean rocks are the primary rocks formed when the molten earth cooled and solidified, so they are the base on which every later system was laid. Being igneous and metamorphic and formed before life flourished, they contain no fossils.
questions.s: NCERT Class XI, India: Physical Environment, Ch 2
questions.h: Order of age: Archaean, Dharwar, Cuddapah, Vindhyan, Gondwana - 'A Dog Can Visit Goa'.

questions.q:
Arrange the following rock systems of India in order of formation, from the oldest to the youngest:
1. Vindhyan system
2. Dharwar system
3. Gondwana system
4. Cuddapah system
questions.e: Dharwar rocks came from erosion of the Archaean base; the Cuddapah basin followed, then the Vindhyan sediments, and the coal-bearing Gondwana sediments are much younger, laid down from the Carboniferous onwards.
questions.s: NCERT Class XI, India: Physical Environment, Ch 2; Majid Husain, Geography of India

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Dharwar system of rocks:
1. They are the first sedimentary rocks of India that were subjected to metamorphism.
2. They are an important source of iron ore, manganese and gold.
3. They are rich in fossils, which help in dating them.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Dharwar sediments were derived from erosion of Archaean rocks and then heavily metamorphosed, which is why they carry minerals such as iron, manganese and gold (Kolar). The same metamorphism destroyed any organic remains, so statement 3 is wrong.
questions.s: Majid Husain, Geography of India, Ch on Geological Structure

questions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the Gondwana system of India:
1. It contains the bulk of India's coal reserves.
2. Its coal is found mainly in the valleys of the Damodar, Mahanadi and Godavari.
3. Its rocks are of marine origin.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Gondwana sediments were laid down by rivers in down-faulted troughs along river valleys, where swampy forests turned into coal. Because they are continental (fluvial) deposits and not marine ones, statement 3 is wrong.
questions.s: NCERT Class XI, India: Physical Environment, Ch 2
questions.h: Gondwana = Gondwana coal, river valley troughs.

questions.q:
Statement-I: The Deccan Trap region is characterised by extensive black cotton (regur) soil.
Statement-II: The Deccan Trap consists of basaltic lava flows whose weathering yields fine-textured, iron-rich clayey soil that retains moisture.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Basalt is rich in iron and magnesium minerals and weathers to a clayey soil that swells when wet and cracks when dry. This direct parent-material link is why regur is concentrated over the Deccan lava plateau.
questions.s: NCERT Class XI, India: Physical Environment, Ch 2; NCERT Class XI Ch 6 (Soils)

questions.q:
How many of the following statements are correct?
1. The Vindhyan system consists largely of unmetamorphosed sedimentary rocks stretching from Sasaram in Bihar to Chittorgarh in Rajasthan.
2. The Cuddapah system is older than the Vindhyan system.
3. Dharwar rocks are rich in fossils and give the earliest record of life in India.
4. The Vindhyan system is an important source of sandstone used as building stone.
questions.e: Vindhyan rocks are largely un-metamorphosed and yield sandstone for building; the Cuddapah system precedes them. Dharwar rocks, being metamorphosed, hold no fossils, so statement 3 is wrong.
questions.s: Majid Husain, Geography of India

questions.q:
Match List-I (Rock system) with List-II (Characteristic) and select the correct answer:
List-I
A. Vindhyan system
B. Deccan Trap
C. Gondwana system
D. Dharwar system
List-II
1. Principal source of India's coal
2. Source of gold, iron ore and manganese
3. Sandstone widely used as building stone
4. Basaltic lava flows weathering into black soil
questions.e: Vindhyan sandstone is the classic building stone; Deccan basalt gives regur; Gondwana basins hold the coal; Dharwar rocks are the metal-bearing ones, with gold at Kolar.
questions.s: NCERT Class XI, India: Physical Environment, Ch 2; Majid Husain, Geography of India

questions.q: Most of India's petroleum reserves, as in Assam, Gujarat and the Mumbai offshore area, are associated with sedimentary basins of which one of the following systems?
questions.e: Oil forms from marine organic matter buried in sedimentary layers and is trapped in anticlines. The Tertiary basins fit this, whereas the crystalline Archaean and heavily metamorphosed Dharwar rocks cannot hold oil.
questions.s: Majid Husain, Geography of India

questions.q: Which one of the following landmasses was NOT a part of the ancient supercontinent Gondwanaland?
questions.e: Pangaea split into northern Laurasia (North America, Greenland, Europe, Asia) and southern Gondwanaland (South America, Africa, Madagascar, India, Australia, Antarctica). Peninsular India later drifted north from Gondwanaland.
questions.s: NCERT Class XI, India: Physical Environment, Ch 2 (Ch 2, Evolution of the Earth); NCERT Class XI Fundamentals of Physical Geography Ch 4

questions.q:
Arrange the following events in India's geological history in chronological order, from the oldest to the youngest:
1. Deccan volcanic eruptions
2. Formation of the Archaean basement rocks
3. Uplift of the Himalaya
4. Deposition of the coal-bearing Gondwana sediments
questions.e: The Archaean basement came first and the Gondwana sediments next. The Deccan eruptions happened as India drifted north near the end of the Cretaceous, and the collision that uplifted the Himalaya came afterwards.
questions.s: NCERT Class XI, India: Physical Environment, Ch 2

questions.q: Which one of the following statements about the Peninsular Plateau is NOT correct?
o: It was once a part of Gondwanaland
It is made up largely of ancient crystalline rocks
The Narmada and Tapi flow westwards through rift valleys along its northern part
It is completely free from earthquakes because it is a very stable block
questions.e: The plateau is old and relatively stable, but stable does not mean immune: the Koyna (1967) and Latur-Killari (1993) earthquakes occurred within it. The word 'completely' is the trap.
questions.s: NCERT Class XI, India: Physical Environment, Ch 2

questions.q:
How many of the following pairs of parent rock and metamorphic rock are correctly matched?
1. Limestone - Marble
2. Shale - Slate
3. Sandstone - Gneiss
4. Basalt - Quartzite
questions.e: Limestone becomes marble and shale becomes slate. Sandstone turns into quartzite, and gneiss comes from granite, so pairs 3 and 4 are wrong.
questions.s: NCERT Class XI Fundamentals of Physical Geography, Ch 5
questions.h: Sand-stone to quartz-ite; granite to gneiss.

questions.q:
Statement-I: The Narmada and Tapi rivers form estuaries and not deltas.
Statement-II: Both rivers flow in narrow rift valleys on a fairly straight course and carry little alluvium.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Flowing through faulted troughs, the two rivers have little room and little silt to spread, so they enter the Arabian Sea through funnel-shaped estuaries.
questions.s: NCERT Class XI, India: Physical Environment, Ch 2; NCERT Class XI Ch 3 (Drainage)

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Geological Survey of India (GSI):
1. It was established in 1851, originally to search for coal for the railways.
2. Its headquarters is at Kolkata.
3. It functions under the Ministry of Earth Sciences.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: GSI is among the oldest geological surveys in the world, set up when railway expansion created demand for coal. It is an attached office of the Ministry of Mines, not of the Ministry of Earth Sciences.
questions.s: Ministry of Mines / GSI official website

questions.q: The occurrence of fossils of the Glossopteris flora in India, Africa, South America, Australia and Antarctica is cited as evidence for which one of the following?
o: Existence of the Tethys Sea over the Himalayan region
Sea-floor spreading along the Mid-Atlantic Ridge only
Former unity of these landmasses in Gondwanaland and continental drift
Uniform climate over the whole globe in the Palaeozoic era
questions.e: Glossopteris was a seed fern that could not cross oceans, so its presence on widely separated continents suggests they were once joined. Wegener used this and the matching Gondwana rock sequences as proof.
questions.s: NCERT Class XI Fundamentals of Physical Geography, Ch 4
questions.h: Plant that cannot swim, yet found on five continents.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Deccan Traps:
1. They were formed by fissure eruptions of basaltic lava.
2. They were formed during the Palaeozoic era.
3. They cover parts of Maharashtra, Gujarat, Madhya Pradesh and Karnataka.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The Deccan Traps are a flood-basalt province built by repeated fissure eruptions around the Cretaceous-Eocene boundary, far younger than the Palaeozoic. They spread over a large part of the northwestern Deccan.
questions.s: NCERT Class XI, India: Physical Environment, Ch 2

questions.q: The Deccan Traps are attributed to the movement of the Indian plate over which one of the following mantle hotspots?
questions.e: As the Indian plate drifted north it passed over the Reunion hotspot, which poured out enormous basalt flows. The Reunion Island volcano in the Indian Ocean is today's surface expression of that hotspot.
questions.s: NCERT Class XI Fundamentals of Physical Geography, Ch 3 and Ch 4

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Himalaya were formed from the sediments of the Tethys geosyncline that were folded and uplifted.
2. The Indian plate was a part of Laurasia before it began its northward drift.
3. The Indo-Gangetic plain occupies a foredeep south of the Himalaya that was filled with sediments.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: As the Indian plate (a Gondwana fragment) pushed north, the Tethys sediments were compressed into the Himalaya and a trough developed to their south, which rivers filled to form the plains. Statement 2 is wrong because India belonged to Gondwanaland.
questions.s: NCERT Class XI, India: Physical Environment, Ch 2
questions.h: Tethys squeezed, mountain rises, trough fills.

questions.q:
Consider the following rocks: 1. Basalt  2. Granite  3. Gabbro  4. Rhyolite
Which of the above are intrusive (plutonic) igneous rocks?
questions.e: Granite and gabbro cool slowly beneath the surface and have coarse crystals. Basalt and rhyolite are extrusive, formed from lava that cooled quickly on the surface.
questions.s: NCERT Class XI Fundamentals of Physical Geography, Ch 5

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Himalayan ranges:
1. The Himadri is the southernmost and the youngest of the three parallel ranges.
2. The Himachal range contains hill stations such as Shimla and Mussoorie.
3. The Shiwaliks are the outermost range of the Himalaya.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: From north to south the ranges are Himadri (Greater), Himachal (Lesser) and Shiwalik, so Himadri is the northernmost, not the southernmost. The Himachal range hosts the hill stations, and the Shiwaliks are the outer, lowest foothills.
questions.s: NCERT Class XI, India: Physical Environment, Ch 2; Majid Husain, Geography of India
questions.h: Himadri is Highest, Himachal is Hill-stations, Shiwalik is Southern foothill.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Duns are longitudinal valleys lying between the Lesser Himalaya and the Shiwaliks.
2. The Shiwaliks are composed of unconsolidated sediments brought down from the higher Himalaya.
3. The Pir Panjal range is a part of the Greater Himalaya.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Rivers eroding the higher ranges deposited loose sediments that make up the Shiwaliks, and duns such as Dehradun lie between them and the Lesser Himalaya. The Pir Panjal is the longest range of the Lesser Himalaya.
questions.s: NCERT Class XI, India: Physical Environment, Ch 2

questions.q:
Match List-I (Pass) with List-II (State) and select the correct answer:
List-I
A. Shipki La
B. Nathu La
C. Bomdi La
D. Lipulekh
List-II
1. Sikkim
2. Himachal Pradesh
3. Arunachal Pradesh
4. Uttarakhand
questions.e: Shipki La is on the Sutlej in Kinnaur (Himachal Pradesh), Nathu La and Jelep La are in Sikkim, Bomdi La is in Arunachal Pradesh and Lipulekh is on the Uttarakhand-Tibet-Nepal tri-junction route to Kailash Mansarovar.
questions.s: NCERT Class XI, India: Physical Environment, Ch 2 (Himalayan passes); Atlas

questions.q: Which one of the following passes is NOT located in Himachal Pradesh?
questions.e: Jelep La lies on the Sikkim-Tibet border near Nathu La. Rohtang and Kunzum La are in Lahaul-Spiti and Kullu, and Shipki La is in Kinnaur.
questions.s: Atlas; NCERT Class XI, India: Physical Environment, Ch 2

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Nanda Devi is the highest peak lying entirely within India.
2. Anamudi is the highest peak of the Western Ghats and of peninsular India.
3. Dhupgarh is the highest peak of the Aravalli range.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Nanda Devi (Uttarakhand) lies wholly in India, while Kanchenjunga is on the Sikkim-Nepal border. Anamudi is in the Anamalai hills of Kerala. Dhupgarh is the highest point of the Satpura range; Guru Shikhar at Mount Abu tops the Aravalli.
questions.s: NCERT Class XI, India: Physical Environment, Ch 2; Atlas
questions.h: Satpura = Dhupgarh (Pachmarhi); Aravalli = Guru Shikhar (Mount Abu).

questions.q:
Match List-I (Division of the Himalaya, Burrard) with List-II (Extent between rivers):
List-I
A. Punjab Himalaya
B. Kumaon Himalaya
C. Nepal Himalaya
D. Assam Himalaya
List-II
1. Kali to Teesta
2. Indus to Sutlej
3. Teesta to Dihang
4. Sutlej to Kali
questions.e: The regional divisions run west to east between river valleys: Indus-Sutlej, Sutlej-Kali, Kali-Teesta, then Teesta-Dihang (Brahmaputra).
questions.s: NCERT Class XI, India: Physical Environment, Ch 2; Majid Husain, Geography of India
questions.h: West to east: I-S, S-K, K-T, T-D (Indus, Sutlej, Kali, Teesta, Dihang).

questions.q: Which one of the following is the correct sequence of the ranges of Kashmir and Ladakh from north to south?
questions.e: The Karakoram, with K2 and Siachen, lies farthest north. South of it come the Ladakh range, then the Zanskar range, and then the Great Himalaya, with the Indus flowing between the Ladakh and Zanskar ranges.
questions.s: NCERT Class XI, India: Physical Environment, Ch 2; Atlas

questions.q:
How many of the following glaciers are correctly paired with their location?
1. Gangotri - Uttarakhand
2. Zemu - Arunachal Pradesh
3. Pindari - Himachal Pradesh
4. Siachen - Karakoram range
questions.e: Gangotri (Uttarakhand) and Siachen (Karakoram) are correctly matched. Zemu is in Sikkim on the Kanchenjunga massif and Pindari is in the Kumaon Himalaya of Uttarakhand.
questions.s: NCERT Class XI, India: Physical Environment, Ch 2; Atlas

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Karewas:
1. They are thick deposits of glacial clay and other material embedded with moraines.
2. They are found in the Kumaon Himalaya.
3. The valley in which they occur lies between the Pir Panjal and the Zanskar ranges.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Karewas are plateau-like deposits in the Kashmir valley, formed when the valley held a lake, and they are useful for saffron (zafran) cultivation. They occur only in the Kashmir Himalaya, not in Kumaon.
questions.s: NCERT Class XI, India: Physical Environment, Ch 2

questions.q: Which one of the following is NOT a part of the Lesser Himalaya (Himachal)?
questions.e: The Karakoram lies in the Trans-Himalaya, north of the Greater Himalaya. Pir Panjal, Dhauladhar and Nag Tibba are ranges of the Lesser Himalaya.
questions.s: NCERT Class XI, India: Physical Environment, Ch 2; Majid Husain, Geography of India

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Northern Plains:
1. The Bhabar is a porous belt of pebbles in which streams disappear.
2. The Terai lies to the north of the Bhabar.
3. Streams re-emerge in the Terai, making it damp and marshy.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Streams drop their coarse load at the foot of the Shiwaliks and sink into the porous Bhabar, then re-emerge further south in the Terai. The Terai therefore lies south of the Bhabar.
questions.s: NCERT Class XI, India: Physical Environment, Ch 2

questions.q:
How many of the following statements are correct?
1. Bhangar is the newer alluvium of the Northern Plains.
2. Khadar is the older alluvium that lies above the flood level.
3. The Bhabar lies to the south of the Terai.
4. Bhangar soil often contains calcareous concretions known as kankar.
questions.e: Bhangar is the older alluvium, forming terraces above flood level and containing kankar. Khadar is the newer, flood-renewed alluvium, and the Bhabar lies north of the Terai, so only statement 4 is correct.
questions.s: NCERT Class XI, India: Physical Environment, Ch 2
questions.h: Bhangar = old, high, kankar; Khadar = new, low, floods.

questions.q: Which one of the following plateaus lies between the Aravalli range in the northwest and the Vindhyan range in the south?
questions.e: The Malwa plateau, largely covered with Deccan lava and black soil, is bounded by the Aravallis on the northwest and the Vindhyas on the south. Chotanagpur is in the east, Telangana in the south, Meghalaya in the northeast.
questions.s: NCERT Class XI, India: Physical Environment, Ch 2

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Western and Eastern Ghats:
1. The Western Ghats are continuous and can be crossed only through passes such as Thal Ghat, Bhor Ghat and Pal Ghat.
2. The Western Ghats have a higher average elevation than the Eastern Ghats.
3. Anamudi lies in the Eastern Ghats.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The Western Ghats form an unbroken escarpment, rising higher than the Eastern Ghats, and Anamudi (Kerala) is their highest peak. The Eastern Ghats are broken by the Godavari, Mahanadi, Krishna and Kaveri.
questions.s: NCERT Class XI, India: Physical Environment, Ch 2

questions.q: The Palghat Gap, a major break in the Western Ghats, lies between which of the following?
questions.e: The Palghat (Palakkad) Gap, about 30 km wide, separates the Nilgiris in the north from the Anamalai, Palani and Cardamom hills in the south, and links Kerala with Tamil Nadu.
questions.s: NCERT Class XI, India: Physical Environment, Ch 2; Atlas

questions.q: Which one of the following is NOT a part of the Eastern Ghats?
questions.e: The Cardamom Hills are in the southern Western Ghats of Kerala and Tamil Nadu. Nallamala, Javadi and Shevaroy hills are discontinuous parts of the Eastern Ghats, which meet the Western Ghats at the Nilgiris.
questions.s: NCERT Class XI, India: Physical Environment, Ch 2; Atlas

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the coastal plains of India:
1. The western coastal plain is narrower than the eastern coastal plain.
2. The eastern coastal plain has well-developed deltas of the Mahanadi, Godavari, Krishna and Kaveri.
3. Rivers of the western coast form large deltas.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The west coast lies between the Western Ghats and the Arabian Sea and is a narrow strip with short, fast rivers that form estuaries. The wide east coast has large deltas built by the east-flowing peninsular rivers.
questions.s: NCERT Class XI, India: Physical Environment, Ch 2

questions.q:
How many of the following lagoons or lakes are correctly paired with their location?
1. Chilika - Odisha
2. Pulicat - Andhra Pradesh and Tamil Nadu
3. Vembanad - Tamil Nadu
4. Kolleru - Karnataka
questions.e: Chilika (Odisha) and Pulicat (on the Andhra Pradesh-Tamil Nadu border) are correct. Vembanad is in Kerala, and Kolleru, a freshwater lake between the Krishna and Godavari deltas, is in Andhra Pradesh.
questions.s: NCERT Class XI, India: Physical Environment, Ch 2; Atlas

questions.q:
How many of the following statements are correct?
1. The Ten Degree Channel separates the Andaman Islands from the Nicobar Islands.
2. The Eight Degree Channel separates Minicoy from the Maldives.
3. Barren Island is the only confirmed active volcano in India.
4. The Lakshadweep islands are of volcanic origin.
questions.e: The channels and Barren Island statements are correct. Lakshadweep islands are coral atolls, not volcanic, so statement 4 is wrong.
questions.s: NCERT Class XI, India: Physical Environment, Ch 2

questions.q: Which one of the following water bodies separates the Indian mainland from Sri Lanka in the north and is separated from the Gulf of Mannar by the chain of shoals known as Adam's Bridge?
questions.e: The Palk Strait lies between Tamil Nadu and Sri Lanka, while the Gulf of Mannar lies to its south. Adam's Bridge (Rama Setu), a chain of limestone shoals running from Pamban island towards Mannar, sits between the two.
questions.s: Atlas; NCERT Class XI, India: Physical Environment, Ch 2

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Meghalaya plateau:
1. It is a detached part of the Peninsular Plateau.
2. It is separated from the Chotanagpur plateau by the Garo-Rajmahal gap.
3. It is composed of the Mizo, Naga and Patkai hills.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The Meghalaya plateau is a block of the old Peninsular mass cut off by the Ganga's deposits filling the Garo-Rajmahal gap. It comprises the Garo, Khasi and Jaintia hills, whereas Mizo, Naga and Patkai belong to Purvanchal.
questions.s: NCERT Class XI, India: Physical Environment, Ch 2

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Thar Desert:
1. Crescent-shaped dunes called barchans are common in it.
2. The Luni, rising in the Aravalli, is the most important river of the region.
3. It lies entirely within Rajasthan.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Barchans are wind-formed crescent dunes, and the ephemeral Luni drains the region towards the Rann of Kachchh. The desert extends beyond Rajasthan into Haryana, Punjab and Gujarat, and across the border into Pakistan.
questions.s: NCERT Class XI, India: Physical Environment, Ch 2

questions.q:
Match the Doabs of the Punjab plains with the rivers between which they lie:
List-I
A. Bari Doab
B. Rechna Doab
C. Chaj Doab
D. Bist Doab
List-II
1. Chenab and Jhelum
2. Beas and Sutlej
3. Beas and Ravi
4. Ravi and Chenab
questions.e: Doab means the land between two rivers. Moving from the Beas westwards, Bari lies between Beas and Ravi, Rechna between Ravi and Chenab, and Chaj between Chenab and Jhelum, while Bist (Bist-Jalandhar) is between Beas and Sutlej.
questions.s: Majid Husain, Geography of India
questions.h: BaRi: Beas-Ravi; ReCh: Ravi-Chenab; ChaJ: Chenab-Jhelum.

questions.q: Which one of the following is the correct order of the divisions of the western coastal plain from north to south?
questions.e: The western coastal plain is divided into the Konkan in the north, the Kannad plain in the middle and the Malabar coast in the south, famous for its lagoons (kayals).
questions.s: NCERT Class XI, India: Physical Environment, Ch 2

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Indira Point, the southernmost point of India, is in Great Nicobar.
2. Barren Island, in the Andaman Sea, is the only confirmed active volcano in India.
3. Narcondam island is an active volcano.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Indira Point lies at the southern tip of Great Nicobar. Barren Island has erupted repeatedly in recent decades, whereas Narcondam is considered a dormant volcano.
questions.s: NCERT Class XI, India: Physical Environment, Ch 2; Atlas

questions.q:
Statement-I: The Aravalli range is among the oldest fold mountains of the world.
Statement-II: The Aravalli range extends in a northeast-southwest direction from Delhi to Palanpur in Gujarat.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Both facts are true, but the extent of the range does not explain its age. The Aravallis are very old, heavily eroded relics of ancient folding.
questions.s: NCERT Class XI, India: Physical Environment, Ch 2

questions.q:
Statement-I: The Eastern Ghats are a discontinuous range.
Statement-II: The Eastern Ghats are cut across by the Narmada and the Tapi.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: The Eastern Ghats are dissected by the Mahanadi, Godavari, Krishna and Kaveri, which flow east. The Narmada and Tapi flow west far to the north, in rift valleys between the Vindhyas and Satpuras.
questions.s: NCERT Class XI, India: Physical Environment, Ch 2

questions.q:
Statement-I: The Lakshadweep islands are of volcanic origin.
Statement-II: The Lakshadweep islands are coral atolls.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Lakshadweep is a group of coral atolls and reefs built by coral polyps, not volcanic mountains. Barren Island in the Andaman Sea is the volcanic example.
questions.s: NCERT Class XI, India: Physical Environment, Ch 2

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Purvanchal hills:
1. They are composed mostly of strong sandstones.
2. The Mizo hills were earlier known as the Lushai hills.
3. The Patkai hills lie along the India-Pakistan border.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Purvanchal (Patkai, Naga, Manipur and Mizo hills) forms India's eastern border with Myanmar and consists chiefly of sandstones. The Patkai hills lie along the India-Myanmar border, not the Pakistan border.
questions.s: NCERT Class XI, India: Physical Environment, Ch 2

questions.q: The western and eastern ends of the Himalaya are marked by sharp southward bends around which pair of peaks?
questions.e: The Indus gorge cuts around Nanga Parbat in the west and the Dihang (Brahmaputra) gorge around Namcha Barwa in the east, marking the syntaxial bends where the range swings south.
questions.s: NCERT Class XI, India: Physical Environment, Ch 2; Majid Husain, Geography of India

questions.q: The Banihal Pass, crossed by a road and rail tunnels linking Jammu with the Kashmir valley, lies in which range?
questions.e: Banihal cuts across the Pir Panjal, the longest range of the Lesser Himalaya, and is the main gateway to the Kashmir valley from the south. Zoji La, in contrast, lies on the Srinagar-Leh route.
questions.s: Atlas; NCERT Class XI, India: Physical Environment, Ch 2
